sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca āyāntaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ dṛṣṭvā gajaḥ pratigajaṃ yathā asaṃbhrāntataraḥ karṇaḥ partyudīyād dhanaṃjayam
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the Pāṇḍava advancing, Karṇa, wholly unshaken, went forth to meet Dhanaṃjaya as one elephant goes forth against another.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena vaikartanam ajihmagaiḥ vārayām āsa tejasvī pāṇḍavaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: As Vaikartana rushed upon him with speed, the radiant Pāṇḍava, scorcher of foes, held him off with straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: taṃ karṇaḥ śarajālena chādayām āsa māriṣa vivyādha ca susaṃkruddhaḥ śarais tribhir ajihmagaiḥ
english: Karṇa, O sire, covered him with a net of arrows, and in his fury pierced him with three straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: tasya tal lāghavaṃ pārtho nāmṛṣyata mahābalaḥ tasmai bāṇāñ śilādhautān prasannāgrān ajihmagān
english: The mighty Pārtha would not endure that nimbleness of his; against him he loosed arrows whetted on stone, bright-tipped and straight-flying.

sanskrit: prāhiṇot sūtaputrāya triṃśataṃ śatrutāpanaḥ vivyādha cainaṃ saṃrabdho bāṇenaikena vīryavān
english: Thirty of them the scorcher of foes sent against the Sūta's son, and the valiant one, enraged, pierced him with a single shaft.

sanskrit: savye bhujāgre balavān nārācena hasann iva tasya viddhasya vegena karāc cāpaṃ papāta ha
english: With an iron shaft, as if smiling, the strong one struck him on the tip of his left arm, and by the force of that wound the bow fell from Karṇa's hand.

sanskrit: punar ādāya tac cāpaṃ nimeṣārdhān mahābalaḥ chādayām āsa bāṇaughaiḥ phalgunaṃ kṛtahastavat
english: Taking up that bow again in half the blink of an eye, the mighty one, deft of hand, covered Phalguna with floods of arrows.

sanskrit: śaravṛṣṭiṃ tu tāṃ muktāṃ sūtaputreṇa bhārata vyadhamac charavarṣeṇa smayann iva dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: But that rain of arrows loosed by the Sūta's son, O Bhārata, Dhanaṃjaya, as if smiling, scattered with a downpour of shafts of his own.

sanskrit: tau parasparam āsādya śaravarṣeṇa pārthiva chādayetāṃ maheṣvāsau kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇau
english: Closing upon each other, O king, those two great archers, each striving to repay the other's stroke, veiled each other with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam abhūd yuddhaṃ karṇapāṇḍavayor mṛdhe kruddhayor vāśitāhetor vanyayor gajayor iva
english: Wondrous was that battle of Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava upon the field, like the fight of two wild elephants enraged over a she-elephant in heat.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho maheṣvāso dṛṣṭvā karṇasya vikramam muṣṭideśe dhanus tasya ciccheda tvarayānvitaḥ
english: Then Pārtha, the great archer, beholding Karṇa's prowess, with all speed cut through his bow at the grip.

sanskrit: aśvāṃś ca caturo bhallair anayad yamasādanam sāratheś ca śiraḥ kāyād aharac chatrutāpanaḥ
english: With broad-headed shafts he sent the four horses to the abode of Yama, and the scorcher of foes struck the charioteer's head from his body.

sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ hatāśvaṃ hatasārathim vivyādha sāyakaiḥ pārthaś caturbhiḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Then him, his bow severed, his horses slain, his charioteer slain, Pārtha, the joy of Pāṇḍu's line, pierced with four arrows.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya nararṣabhaḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ kṛpasya śarapīḍitaḥ
english: Swiftly leaping down from the car whose horses were slain, that bull among men, sore pressed by arrows, swiftly mounted Kṛpa's chariot.

sanskrit: rādheyaṃ nirjitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tāvakā bharatarṣabha dhanaṃjayaśarair nunnāḥ prādravanta diśo daśa
english: Seeing Rādheya defeated, O bull of the Bhāratas, your men, driven by Dhanaṃjaya's arrows, fled in all ten directions.

sanskrit: dravatas tān samālokya rājā duryodhano nṛpa nivartayām āsa tadā vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: Beholding them in flight, King Duryodhana, O sovereign, turned them back and spoke these words.

sanskrit: alaṃ drutena vaḥ śūrās tiṣṭhadhvaṃ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ eṣa pārthavadhāyāhaṃ svayaṃ gacchāmi saṃyuge ahaṃ pārthān haniṣyāmi sapāñcālān sasomakān
english: Enough of flight, you heroes! Stand fast, you bulls among Kṣatriyas! Lo, I myself go into the battle to slay Pārtha; I shall slay the Pārthas together with the Pāñcālas and the Somakas.

sanskrit: adya me yudhyamānasya saha gāṇḍīvadhanvanā drakṣyanti vikramaṃ pārthāḥ kālasyeva yugakṣaye
english: This day, as I fight against the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, the Pārthas shall behold my valor, like that of Time at the dissolution of an age.

sanskrit: adya madbāṇajālāni vimuktāni sahasraśaḥ drakṣyanti samare yodhāḥ śalabhānām ivāyatīḥ
english: This day the warriors shall behold in the battle the nets of my arrows loosed by the thousand, like advancing swarms of locusts.

sanskrit: adya bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ sṛjato mama dhanvinaḥ jīmūtasyeva gharmānte drakṣyanti yudhi sainikāḥ
english: This day the soldiers shall behold in the fight the arrowy rain poured forth by me, the bowman, like a thundercloud's at the close of the hot season.

sanskrit: jeṣyāmy adya raṇe pārthaṃ sāyakair nataparvabhiḥ tiṣṭhadhvaṃ samare śūrā bhayaṃ tyajata phalgunāt
english: This day in battle I shall conquer Pārtha with smooth-jointed shafts. Stand fast in the fight, you heroes; cast away your fear of Phalguna.

sanskrit: na hi madvīryam āsādya phalgunaḥ prasahiṣyati yathā velāṃ samāsādya sāgaro makarālayaḥ
english: For having met my might, Phalguna shall not prevail over it, even as the sea, abode of sea-monsters, prevails not against the shore it meets.

sanskrit: ity uktvā prayayau rājā sainyena mahatā vṛtaḥ phalgunaṃ prati durdharṣaḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the king, hard to assail, his eyes red with wrath, advanced toward Phalguna, encircled by a great host.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ mahābāhuṃ dṛṣṭvā śāradvatas tadā aśvatthāmānam āsādya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Seeing that mighty-armed one set forth, Śāradvata then approached Aśvatthāman and spoke these words.

sanskrit: eṣa rājā mahābāhur amarṣī krodhamūrchitaḥ pataṃgavṛttim āsthāya phalgunaṃ yoddhum icchati
english: This mighty-armed king, full of indignation, swooning with wrath, has taken up the way of the moth toward the flame and seeks to fight Phalguna.

sanskrit: yāvan naḥ paśyamānānāṃ prāṇān pārthena saṃgataḥ na jahyāt puruṣavyāghras tāvad vāraya kauravam
english: Before this tiger among men, having closed with Pārtha, yields up his life beneath our very eyes, restrain the Kaurava.

sanskrit: yāvat phalgunabāṇānāṃ gocaraṃ nādhigacchati kauravaḥ pārthivo vīras tāvad vāraya taṃ drutam
english: Before the heroic Kaurava king comes within range of Phalguna's arrows, restrain him at once.

sanskrit: yāvat pārthaśarair ghorair nirmuktoragasaṃnibhaiḥ na bhasmīkriyate rājā tāvad yuddhān nivāryatām
english: Before the king is reduced to ashes by Pārtha's dreadful arrows, like serpents loosed from their slough, let him be turned back from the battle.

sanskrit: ayuktam iva paśyāmi tiṣṭhatsv asmāsu mānada svayaṃ yuddhāya yad rājā pārthaṃ yāty asahāyavān
english: It seems unfitting to me, O giver of honor, that while we stand here the king should go alone, unaided, to fight Pārtha.

sanskrit: durlabhaṃ jīvitaṃ manye kauravyasya kirīṭinā yudhyamānasya pārthena śārdūleneva hastinaḥ
english: Hard to keep, I deem, is the life of the Kaurava, fighting against the diademed Pārtha, as is an elephant's against a tiger.

sanskrit: mātulenaivam uktas tu drauṇiḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ duryodhanam idaṃ vākyaṃ tvaritaṃ samabhāṣata
english: Thus addressed by his uncle, Drauṇi, foremost of weapon-bearers, spoke in haste these words to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: mayi jīvati gāndhāre na yuddhaṃ gantum arhasi mām anādṛtya kauravya tava nityaṃ hitaiṣiṇam
english: While I live, O son of Gāndhārī, you ought not to go into battle, slighting me, O Kaurava, who am ever a seeker of your good.

sanskrit: na hi te saṃbhramaḥ kāryaḥ pārthasya vijayaṃ prati aham āvārayiṣyāmi pārthaṃ tiṣṭha suyodhana
english: You need feel no alarm for Pārtha's victory; I shall hold Pārtha off. Stay back, Suyodhana.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ācāryaḥ pāṇḍuputrān vai putravat parirakṣati tvam apy upekṣāṃ kuruṣe teṣu nityaṃ dvijottama
english: Duryodhana said: The teacher guards the sons of Pāṇḍu as though they were his own children, and you too, O best of the twice-born, ever show indifference toward them.

sanskrit: mama vā mandabhāgyatvān mandas te vikramo yudhi dharmarājapriyārthaṃ vā draupadyā vā na vidma tat
english: Whether your prowess in battle is feeble through my own ill fortune, or for the sake of pleasing the Dharma-king, or of Draupadī—that I do not know.

sanskrit: dhig astu mama lubdhasya yatkṛte sarvabāndhavāḥ sukhārhāḥ paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpnuvanty aparājitāḥ
english: Fie upon me, the greedy one, for whose sake all these kinsmen, deserving of joy and unconquered, are come to the utmost grief!

sanskrit: ko hi śastrabhṛtāṃ mukhyo maheśvarasamo yudhi śatrūn na kṣapayec chakto yo na syād gautamīsutaḥ
english: For what foremost of weapon-bearers, equal in battle to Maheśvara, being able, would not destroy his foes—unless he were the son of Gautamī?

sanskrit: aśvatthāman prasīdasva nāśayaitān mamāhitān tavāstragocare śaktāḥ sthātuṃ devāpi nānagha
english: Aśvatthāman, be gracious; destroy these enemies of mine. Within range of your weapons not even the gods are able to stand, O sinless one.

sanskrit: pāñcālān somakāṃś caiva jahi drauṇe sahānugān vayaṃ śeṣān haniṣyāmas tvayaiva parirakṣitāḥ
english: Slay the Pāñcālas and the Somakas with their followers, O Drauṇi; the rest we shall slay, guarded by you alone.

sanskrit: ete hi somakā vipra pāñcālāś ca yaśasvinaḥ mama sainyeṣu saṃrabdhā vicaranti davāgnivat
english: For these Somakas, O Brahman, and the glorious Pāñcālas, in their fury range through my armies like a forest fire.

sanskrit: tān vāraya mahābāho kekayāṃś ca narottama purā kurvanti niḥśeṣaṃ rakṣyamāṇāḥ kirīṭinā
english: Hold them back, O mighty-armed, and the Kekayas too, O best of men, before, guarded by the diademed one, they leave nothing of us remaining.

sanskrit: ādau vā yadi vā paścāt tavedaṃ karma māriṣa tvam utpanno mahābāho pāñcālānāṃ vadhaṃ prati
english: Whether at the first or at the last, this deed is yours, O sire; you were born, O mighty-armed, for the slaughter of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: kariṣyasi jagat sarvam apāñcālaṃ kilācyuta evaṃ siddhābruvan vāco bhaviṣyati ca tat tathā
english: You shall make the whole world free of Pāñcālas, O imperishable one; thus have the perfected ones spoken, and so shall it surely come to pass.

sanskrit: na te 'stragocare śaktāḥ sthātuṃ devāḥ savāsavāḥ kim u pārthāḥ sapāñcālāḥ satyam etad vaco mama
english: Within range of your weapons the gods themselves with Vāsava are unable to stand—how much less the Pārthas with the Pāñcālas? This word of mine is the truth.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duryodhanenaivam ukto drauṇir āhavadurmadaḥ pratyuvāca mahābāho yathā vadasi kaurava
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus addressed by Duryodhana, Drauṇi, fierce in battle, replied: "It is as you say, O mighty-armed Kaurava."

sanskrit: priyā hi pāṇḍavā nityaṃ mama cāpi pituś ca me tathaivāvāṃ priyau teṣāṃ na tu yuddhe kurūdvaha śaktitas tāta yudhyāmas tyaktvā prāṇān abhītavat
english: Dear indeed are the Pāṇḍavas ever to me and to my father, and dear likewise are we two to them; yet not in war, O chief of the Kurus. With all our strength, my friend, we fight, casting away our lives without fear.

sanskrit: ahaṃ karṇaś ca śalyaś ca kṛpo hārdikya eva ca nimeṣāt pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ kṣapayema nṛpottama
english: I, and Karṇa, and Śalya, and Kṛpa, and Hārdikya too—in the twinkling of an eye we could destroy the Pāṇḍava host, O best of kings.

sanskrit: te cāpi kauravīṃ senāṃ nimeṣārdhāt kurūdvaha kṣapayeyur mahābāho na syāma yadi saṃyuge
english: And they too could destroy the Kaurava host in half the twinkling of an eye, O chief of the Kurus, mighty-armed one, were we not present in the battle.

sanskrit: yudhyatāṃ pāṇḍavāñ śaktyā teṣāṃ cāsmān yuyutsatām tejas tu teja āsādya praśamaṃ yāti bhārata
english: We fight the Pāṇḍavas with all our power, and they would fight us; yet when energy meets energy, O Bhārata, it comes to a standstill.

sanskrit: aśakyā tarasā jetuṃ pāṇḍavānām anīkinī jīvatsu pāṇḍuputreṣu tad dhi satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: The army of the Pāṇḍavas cannot be conquered by mere onset while the sons of Pāṇḍu live—this truth I tell you.

sanskrit: ātmārthaṃ yudhyamānās te samarthāḥ pāṇḍunandanāḥ kimarthaṃ tava sainyāni na haniṣyanti bhārata
english: Fighting for their own cause, the able sons of Pāṇḍu—why should they not slay your armies, O Bhārata?

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi lubdhatamo rājan nikṛtijñaś ca kaurava sarvātiśaṅkī mānī ca tato 'smān atiśaṅkase
english: For you, O king, are most greedy, and skilled in deceit, O Kaurava, suspicious of everyone and proud; therefore you mistrust us also.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu yatnam āsthāya tvadarthe tyaktajīvitaḥ eṣa gacchāmi saṃgrāmaṃ tvatkṛte kurunandana
english: But I, putting forth my utmost effort for your sake, having cast away my life, here go into the battle for you, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: yotsye 'haṃ śatrubhiḥ sārdhaṃ jeṣyāmi ca varān varān pāñcālaiḥ saha yotsyāmi somakaiḥ kekayais tathā pāṇḍaveyaiś ca saṃgrāme tvatpriyārtham ariṃdama
english: I shall fight with the foes and conquer the very best of them; I shall fight with the Pāñcālas, with the Somakas and the Kekayas, and with the sons of Pāṇḍu in battle, to please you, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: adya madbāṇanirdagdhāḥ pāñcālāḥ somakās tathā siṃhenevārditā gāvo vidraviṣyanti sarvataḥ
english: This day, scorched by my arrows, the Pāñcālas and the Somakas shall scatter in every direction, like cattle harried by a lion.

sanskrit: adya dharmasuto rājā dṛṣṭvā mama parākramam aśvatthāmamayaṃ lokaṃ maṃsyate saha somakaiḥ
english: This day, beholding my prowess, King Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, together with the Somakas, shall deem the whole world to be made of Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: āgamiṣyati nirvedaṃ dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dṛṣṭvā vinihatān saṃkhye pāñcālān somakaiḥ saha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, shall come to despair, beholding the Pāñcālas slain in battle together with the Somakas.

sanskrit: ye māṃ yuddhe 'bhiyotsyanti tān haniṣyāmi bhārata na hi te vīra mucyeran madbāhvantaram āgatāḥ
english: Whoever shall fight against me in battle, them I shall slay, O Bhārata; for those heroes, once come within the reach of my arms, would not escape.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhuḥ putraṃ duryodhanaṃ tava abhyavartata yuddhāya drāvayan sarvadhanvinaḥ cikīrṣus tava putrāṇāṃ priyaṃ prāṇabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Having thus spoken to your son Duryodhana, the mighty-armed one turned to the fight, putting all the bowmen to flight—that best of living beings, eager to do your sons a kindness.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt sakaikeyān pāñcālān gautamīsutaḥ praharadhvam itaḥ sarve mama gātre mahārathāḥ sthirībhūtāś ca yudhyadhvaṃ darśayanto 'stralāghavam
english: Then the son of Gautamī addressed the Pāñcālas with the Kekayas: "Strike all of you here upon my body, you great chariot-warriors; stand firm and fight, displaying your deftness with weapons."

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te sarve śastravṛṣṭim apātayan drauṇiṃ prati mahārāja jalaṃ jaladharā iva
english: Thus addressed, they all let fall a rain of weapons upon Drauṇi, O great king, as rain-clouds pour down water.

sanskrit: tān nihatya śarān drauṇir daśa vīrān apothayat pramukhe pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cābhibho
english: Striking down those arrows, Drauṇi crushed ten warriors before the very faces of the sons of Pāṇḍu and of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O lord.

sanskrit: te hanyamānāḥ samare pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayās tathā parityajya raṇe drauṇiṃ vyadravanta diśo daśa
english: Being slain in the battle, the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas forsook Drauṇi on the field and fled in all ten directions.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā dravataḥ śūrān pāñcālān sahasomakān dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja drauṇim abhyadravad yudhi
english: Seeing those heroic Pāñcālas with the Somakas in flight, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, rushed upon Drauṇi in the fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanacitrāṇāṃ sajalāmbudanādinām vṛtaḥ śatena śūrāṇāṃ rathānām anivartinām
english: Then, surrounded by a hundred chariots of heroes who never turned back, gleaming with gold and roaring like rain-laden clouds—

sanskrit: putraḥ pāñcālarājasya dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ drauṇim ity abravīd vākyaṃ dṛṣṭvā yodhān nipātitān
english: the son of the Pāñcāla king, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the great chariot-warrior, beholding his warriors struck down, spoke these words to Drauṇi.

sanskrit: ācāryaputra durbuddhe kim anyair nihatais tava samāgaccha mayā sārdhaṃ yadi śūro 'si saṃyuge ahaṃ tvāṃ nihaniṣyāmi tiṣṭhedānīṃ mamāgrataḥ
english: "O evil-minded son of the teacher, what is it to you that others are slain? Close with me, if you are a hero in battle. I shall slay you—stand now before me!"

sanskrit: tatas tam ācāryasutaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pratāpavān marmabhidbhiḥ śarais tīkṣṇair jaghāna bharatarṣabha
english: Then the valorous Dhṛṣṭadyumna struck that son of the teacher with sharp shafts that pierce the vital parts, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: te tu paṅktīkṛtā drauṇiṃ śarā viviśur āśugāḥ rukmapuṅkhāḥ prasannāgrāḥ sarvakāyāvadāraṇāḥ madhvarthina ivoddāmā bhramarāḥ puṣpitaṃ drumam
english: Those swift arrows, ranged in rows, gold-feathered and bright-tipped, rending the whole body, entered into Drauṇi, like unbridled bees seeking honey upon a flowering tree.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ padākrānta ivoragaḥ mānī drauṇir asaṃbhrānto bāṇapāṇir abhāṣata
english: Sorely pierced and greatly enraged, like a serpent trodden underfoot, the proud Drauṇi, unshaken, arrow in hand, spoke.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumna sthiro bhūtvā muhūrtaṃ pratipālaya yāvat tvāṃ niśitair bāṇaiḥ preṣayāmi yamakṣayam
english: "Dhṛṣṭadyumna, stand firm and wait a moment, while with whetted arrows I send you to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: drauṇir evam athābhāṣya pārṣataṃ paravīrahā chādayām āsa bāṇaughaiḥ samantāl laghuhastavat
english: Having spoken thus to the son of Pṛṣata, Drauṇi, slayer of hostile heroes, deft of hand, covered him on every side with floods of arrows.

sanskrit: sa chādyamānaḥ samare drauṇinā yuddhadurmadaḥ drauṇiṃ pāñcālatanayo vāgbhir ātarjayat tadā
english: Being thus veiled in battle by Drauṇi, the son of the Pāñcāla king, fierce in war, then assailed Drauṇi with taunting words.

sanskrit: na jānīṣe pratijñāṃ me viprotpattiṃ tathaiva ca droṇaṃ hatvā kila mayā hantavyas tvaṃ sudurmate tatas tvāhaṃ na hanmy adya droṇe jīvati saṃyuge
english: "You know not my vow, nor yet my birth from a Brahman: when I have slain Droṇa, then you too are to be slain by me, O most evil-minded one. Therefore I slay you not today, while Droṇa yet lives, in the battle."

sanskrit: imāṃ tu rajanīṃ prāptām aprabhātāṃ sudurmate nihatya pitaraṃ te 'dya tatas tvām api saṃyuge neṣyāmi mṛtyulokāyety evaṃ me manasi sthitam
english: "But upon this night now come, before it dawns, O most evil-minded one, having slain your father this day, then you too in battle I shall lead to the realm of the dead—thus is it fixed in my mind."

sanskrit: yas te pārtheṣu vidveṣo yā bhaktiḥ kauraveṣu ca tāṃ darśaya sthiro bhūtvā na me jīvan vimokṣyase
english: "What hatred you bear toward the Pārthas, what devotion toward the Kauravas—show it, standing firm; you shall not escape me with your life."

sanskrit: yo hi brāhmaṇyam utsṛjya kṣatradharmarato dvijaḥ sa vadhyaḥ sarvalokasya yathā tvaṃ puruṣādhama
english: "For that twice-born man who, forsaking his Brahmanhood, takes delight in the duties of a Kṣatriya, deserves to be slain by all the world—as do you, O basest of men."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ pārṣatena dvijottamaḥ krodham āhārayat tīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Thus addressed with harsh speech by the son of Pṛṣata, that best of the twice-born gathered fierce wrath and cried, "Stand, stand!"

sanskrit: nirdahann iva cakṣurbhyāṃ pārṣataṃ so 'bhyavaikṣata chādayām āsa ca śarair niḥśvasan pannago yathā
english: As if consuming him with his eyes, he gazed upon the son of Pṛṣata, and, hissing like a serpent, covered him with arrows.

sanskrit: sa chādyamānaḥ samare drauṇinā rājasattama sarvapāñcālasenābhiḥ saṃvṛto rathasattamaḥ
english: Being thus veiled in battle by Drauṇi, O best of kings, that best of chariot-warriors stood encompassed by all the Pāñcāla armies.
